item.title: Hugo Site Build Lifecycle
item.description: Hugo builds a site from configuration, mounted files, content metadata, templates, and resources. File placement is part of the data model because it determines page kind, bundle boundaries, and template lookup.

item.title: Hugo Templates and Shortcodes
item.description: Hugo templates combine Go’s template language with Hugo functions and page objects. Shortcodes use the same language, but content authors invoke them from Markdown while Hugo constructs .Content.

item.title: Go Language and Templates
item.description:
Go organizes source into packages and modules, reports recoverable failures as values, and provides reflection-based text and HTML templates in its standard library. The same design principle connects these areas: make dependencies and control flow explicit at the API boundary.

Modules, Packages, and Builds #

A package is the compilation and namespace boundary formed by non-test .go files with the same package declaration in one directory. A module is a versioned collection of packages rooted at go.mod. The module path supplies the import-path prefix:
